dedupe_keys.name: resq ios seismic resilience of interdependent power gas and water networks in shelby county tennessee

description: This study introduces ResQ-IOS, a resilience quantification framework based on iterative optimisation and simulation for interdependent critical infrastructure systems exposed to natural hazards, able to reflect the real-world status of system components. The framework has five modules: risk assessment, simulation, optimisation, database and controller. It was demonstrated on the seismic resilience of interdependent power, natural gas and water networks in Shelby County, Tennessee. Results suggest the water network is the best candidate for pre-disaster resilience enhancement measures such as added supply capacity, while, because the power network controls community recovery, recovery-phase measures such as more repair and maintenance teams should target power to shorten restoration. The authors suggest the tool for resilience-oriented planning, including renewable energy strategies. Licence (read on the provider page on 2026-09-28): CC-BY-4.0. Caveats: the framework code is not released with the paper, and results depend on the Shelby County testbed data and assumed repair resources. It illustrates cascading failure, optimisation and recovery modelling for resilience planning; a related record is the IN-CORE platform. Access is through the provider page linked in this record.
